title: Comfort of Scripture
definition: The comfort of Scripture is the encouragement, hope, correction, and peace God gives His people through His Word in weakness, grief, fear, and trial.
summary: Scripture comforts not by denying pain, but by revealing God's presence, promises, purposes, and final victory.
christFocus: Christ comforts His people as the suffering Savior, risen Lord, and Shepherd who speaks peace through His Word.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content: Comfort of Scripture teaches that God's people must receive this truth under the authority of the Lord, allowing Scripture itself to define the doctrine rather than personal opinion, tradition, or culture.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: This doctrine matters because it protects the believer from confusion and helps the church remain anchored in what God has actually spoken. Without this truth, faith can drift toward feelings, assumptions, or human wisdom.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: A disciple should respond to comfort of scripture by reading the Word prayerfully, testing beliefs by Scripture, obeying what God reveals, and helping others handle the Bible with humility, clarity, and faith.

studySections.heading: Guardrails and Common Errors
studySections.content: This doctrine should not be used to win arguments while neglecting love, nor should it be separated from prayer, obedience, and dependence on the Holy Spirit. The goal is faithful submission to God, not mere possession of information.

sources: Scripture references listed in this doctrine entry.
